questions.title: Seagull moves your golf ball
questions.question: A seagull comes and moves your golf ball from where it was on the fairway. What should you do?

choices.text: Play the ball from where the seagull dropped it
Put the ball back where it was, with no penalty
Add a penalty and put the ball back

questions.explanation: If a seagull (or any animal) moves your ball, you must put it back where it was before, and you don’t get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The short grass part of a golf hole, between the tee and the green.
Extra shots added to your score for breaking a rule.
Something not part of the game, like an animal or a person, that moves your ball.

questions.teachingTip: Explain that only the player or their partner can get a penalty for moving the ball, but animals don’t cause a penalty. Practise putting the ball back on its spot.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children may think they have to play the ball from wherever it ends up after an animal moves it.
Some may think a penalty is given even if an animal moves the ball.

questions.title: Ball moved by a seagull
questions.question: A seagull moves your ball from its spot on the fairway. What should you do under the Rules?

choices.text: Play the ball from where it stopped
Replace the ball where it was with no penalty
Add a penalty and replace the ball

questions.explanation: If your ball at rest is moved by an outside influence, such as a seagull, you must replace it on its original spot with no penalty.
